column1: # The fixture directory of each architecture, the one table of it: crates/refset/src/fixture.rs reads it (include_str!: `dir_of`,
# `first_shard_in`; the registry's test in crates/model/src/arch/registry.rs holds each fixture row's family to it), tools/ref/ref-paths.sh reads it by awk (the
# fixture tier's model file), tools/refset-publish.sh and tools/check-recipes.sh read it by awk too.
#   arch   the BLOOMERY_MODEL profile name, which is the GGUF general.architecture of the fixture's file
#   dir    the directory under the fixture root ($BLOOMERY_FIXTURE_ROOT, default /models/fixtures) holding the fixture's shards, the
#          one name `fixture fetch` takes as its family; lower-case letters, digits and `-`. `self` is not a directory: the family
#          has no fixture file, a command runs on the profile's file and the gate fence (Tier::check_file) refuses that file as not
#          a fixture. An architecture this table does not name has no fixture yet (ref-paths.sh exits 66, never a run on the real file).
#          A directory that holds model.safetensors.index.json is a checkpoint folder cut in its stored bits (`fixture cut`, its rules
#          tools/fixture-cuts/<dir>.json), its first shard the `*-00001-of-*.safetensors` beside the index; any other holds GGUF shards
#          A row no registry row names (a gate profile, not an architecture string) is a profile's cut, listed in `PROFILE_CUTS`
#          of crates/model/src/arch/registry.rs; only the gate clauses that name that cut read it.
